title: LLM failure-mode economic impact simulator and governance playbook
creator: Sofia Martínez
description:
Background: Enterprise customers are asking for quantitative evidence of downstream business impact when a model variant becomes unavailable, underperforms, or regresses. Sales and CSM teams need a concise, reproducible way to show procurement committees the dollar-and-latency impact across fallback strategies (hosted -> dedicated -> private; quantized variants; regional routing).

Scope: Build a lightweight simulator and an associated governance playbook that combines: (1) sampled workload telemetry (token mix, latency percentiles, QPS), (2) model availability scenarios (partial outage, increased tail latency, quality regression), and (3) procurement/contract parameters (SLA tiers, burst capacity cost, reserved capacity amortization). The simulator should output scenario-level metrics: incremental monthly cost, 95th latency uplift, estimated percentage of failed/ downgraded requests, and an enterprise-facing "resilience score".

Goals:
- Provide Sales and Solutions with a one-page decision artifact for procurement conversations.
- Quantify trade-offs between choosing Reserved Dedicated capacity vs hosted with multi-region fallbacks.
- Inform PM/Eng about which mitigations yield best ROI for each vertical (finserv, health, gov).

Out of scope for this ticket: full integration into Console billing UI, legal contract text, or an exhaustive model-compatibility matrix. Those will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator accepts configuration inputs: workload profile (tokens/min, embedding vs gen mix), model availability delta, and procurement parameters
ProducesJSON report with: cost delta/month, 95th latency delta, %requests affected, resilience score
One-pager decision artifact template created and approved by Sales and Solutions (sign-off from lead CSM)
Playbook includes clear mitigation steps mapped to engineering work items and contractual levers
Simulation reproducible from a Jupyter notebook and runnable by solutions engineering without infra changes
deliverables: Jupyter simulator notebook (workload + cost model) in Drive
Consolidated one-page decision artifact template (PDF) for procurement meetings
Governance playbook (Confluence) with runbooks for outages, regression detection triggers, and procurement triggers
Internal slide deck summarizing top-5 vertical-specific recommendations
Tickets created in ENG backlog for top-3 engineering mitigations
timeline: Week 1: collect telemetry and procurement parameters (Feb 10 - Feb 16). Week 2-3: prototype simulator and baseline scenarios (Feb 17 - Mar 2). Week 4: internal review with Sales/CS and iterate (Mar 3 - Mar 9). Week 5: finalize one-pager, playbook, and create ENG tickets (Mar 10 - Mar 16). Stretch: run pilot with 2 enterprise accounts (Mar 17 - Apr 1).
